title: Part
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees and a translation vector also set to zero. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on the first face. In this sketch, start by drawing the first line from the origin (0.0, 0.0) to (0.75, 0.0). Then, draw the second line from (0.75, 0.0) to (0.75, 0.006), followed by the third line from (0.75, 0.006) to (0.0, 0.006). Finally, complete the loop by drawing the fourth line from (0.0, 0.006) back to the origin (0.0, 0.0). After completing the sketch, apply a scale factor of 0.75 to the entire sketch to adjust its size. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into three dimensions by rotating it with Euler angles set to zero degrees and translating it with a vector also set to zero. To generate the three-dimensional model, extrude the sketch 0.0015 units along the normal direction. Ensure that the extrusion does not occur in the opposite direction and that it creates a new solid body. The final dimensions of the part are 0.75 units in length, 0.006 units in width, and 0.0015 units in height.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the sketch
sketch = cq.Workplane("XY").moveTo(0, 0).lineTo(0.75, 0).lineTo(0.75, 0.006).lineTo(0, 0.006).close()

# Extrude the sketch
extrusion = sketch.extrude(0.0015)

# Assign the final model to 'r'
r = extrusion

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.006, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.006, 0.0015) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0015) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90.0, 0.0, -90.0) and the translation vector is (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the object 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)
